questionText: How does Ternary Search divide the search space, and how many comparisons does it perform per step?

options.text: It searches three separate sorted lists in parallel, requiring three independent pointers for each
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: It partitions the interval based on prime number indices, evaluating three prime candidates sequentially
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: It divides the sorted range into 3 equal parts using two midpoints, performing up to 2 comparisons per step
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT principle for Ternary Search Comparison.

options.text: It splits the array into 10 equal segments using nine midpoints, performing up to 9 comparisons per step
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Section B1: Computer Science Core (Ternary Search Comparison):
It divides the sorted range into 3 equal parts using two midpoints, performing up to 2 comparisons per step

Detailed Analysis:
Ternary search splits the search interval into three segments with two midpoints (m1, m2), eliminating 2/3 of the space per step.
Therefore, option (C) is the correct answer.
